claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperature.
Pack-cementation aluminizing will diffuse aluminum into the near-surface region of cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminizing treatment will promote formation of an Al2O3 scale on HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature oxidation.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be thin and continuous.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be coherent and adherent to the alloy.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Slower oxygen ingress will reduce oxidation of the bulk alloy.
The aluminizing treatment will enhance the alloy's oxygen resistance at 1000 °C in air for approximately 50 hours.
The aluminizing treatment will not significantly alter the bulk microstructure controlling ductility and high-temperature strength.
After aluminizing and oxidation exposure, room-temperature tensile ductility will remain approximately within the untreated range of 8–16%.
After aluminizing and oxidation exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 will remain approximately within the untreated range of 163–530 MPa.
The treatment's effectiveness may not persist for longer exposures, extreme thermal cycling, or temperatures significantly above 1000 °C.
